$comment: Managed settings template for fleet deployment. Place at: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json (macOS), /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (Linux/WSL), or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json (Windows). Managed settings cannot be overridden by users or projects. Replace <ORG-MARKETPLACE-URL> with your internal marketplace git URL or path.
$comment_allowManagedHooksOnly: Set allowManagedHooksOnly to true for maximum lockdown: only hooks from managed settings and managed plugins run, so users cannot add hooks that interfere with the guardrails. Test with your developers' existing hooks first.

env.$comment_env: Fleet-wide guardrail tuning. AGW_LEVEL picks an enforcement bundle; the default (omit it) is 'standard'. Strict also redirects every recursive raw discovery through bounded AGW; standard/relaxed allow narrow project-local forms but redirect broad scopes. AGW_STRICT_DISCOVERY overrides that behavior independently. Other individual knobs (AGW_SESSION_MEMORY, AGW_REGENERABLE_RM, AGW_RELAXED_ACCESS, AGW_ENFORCEMENT) override the level. Archive retention is bounded at 4 GiB by default. At the 90% high-water mark Guardrails may automatically prune only eligible cache-like redundant copies toward the 80% low-water mark; restore-critical copies remain protected.
env.$comment_AGW_ARCHIVE_WATERMARKS: Optional byte overrides: AGW_ARCHIVE_HIGH_WATER_BYTES and AGW_ARCHIVE_LOW_WATER_BYTES. When omitted they derive as 90% and 80% of AGW_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES. Set AGW_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES to 0 for explicit unlimited retention; watermarks must then be omitted or zero.
env.$comment_AGW_STRICT_DISCOVERY: Optional boolean override. true redirects every recursive raw rg/grep/find/fd/tree/listing and native Glob/Grep request to bounded agw list/search even outside strict level.
env.$comment_AGW_HOME: The machine-wide archive/session store. Defaults to ~/.agw. Point it at a persistent, NON-cloud-synced path. IMPORTANT on ephemeral/remote runners: if hooks run in a per-session VM whose home (~) is wiped on teardown, ~/.agw does not persist there — set AGW_HOME to a mounted persistent volume.

$comment_optional_hardening: Optionally also pin permissions at the managed level, e.g.: "permissions": { "deny": ["Bash(rm:*)", "Bash(sudo:*)"] } — the plugin's hooks already cover these with better redirects, but managed permission rules add defense in depth that survives even plugin removal.
